full.text:
The Keeper lit the old stone lantern at the edge of the forest every evening. The lantern was the brightest light in the valley and rather proud of itself too. One night a firefly came to rest on the lantern, drawn in by the magnificent flame.

“Your light is very beautiful,” the firefly said.

The lantern scoffed. “Yes, of course it is beautiful,” it said. “You will not find a brighter light for miles around. I have saved many a valley traveler and all who see me are grateful. Your little spark is nothing compared to me.”

“You are right of course,” the firefly replied. “I cannot hope to compare with your brightness, but even small lights should shine wherever they can.”

Later that evening, a violent storm began. The lantern swayed in the howling wind and a fallen branch cracked its glass and snuffed its flame. The winds and fallen trees prevented the Keeper from being able to relight it and the valley was bathed in darkness.

Down in the forest, a young hare was trapped at a fork in the trees. He was carrying medicine for his sick mother and could not find the safe path home among the flooded trees. The lantern could hear the hare’s distress and tried desperately to ignite its own flame. Suddenly, the firefly appeared before the hare, joined by a swarm of other fireflies who helped the hare find its way home by their collective glow. The lantern watched the fireflies with growing shame at its inability to help and boastful behavior.

The next morning, the Keeper repaired the lantern and relit its flame by night. The firefly returned to the lantern, hesitant.

“Please do not be afraid, firefly,” the lantern said. “I saw how you helped the hare last night and I am so sorry for dismissing you. I was wrong to boast. The most meaningful light is that which is provided in moments of need.”

The firefly settled on the rim of the lantern. “I forgive you, friend,” it said.

The lantern dimmed its flame, allowing the glow of the firefly to be seen as well. From that day on, travelers to the forest always saw two lights shining from the hill and the lantern never again mistook greatness with size.

cases_intro.t: A document's prose and ideas can each come from a person or an AI model, giving the following four cases:

cases.def: A person wrote the prose and came up with the ideas.
A person wrote, in their own words, from a model's ideas.
A model wrote the prose and came up with the ideas.
A person came up with the ideas, and a model wrote, rewrote, or polished the prose.
